elements.name: Harness Interface Endpoint
elements.note: TLS 1.3 loopback harness listener, POST-only MCP endpoint, header and body bounds, Host and Origin checks, per-source rate limits and lockout on the OAuth and session endpoints with bounded source tables (IPv6 counted per /64). In the 2026-07-28 era an unknown method gets HTTP 404 with -32601 (FR-1.10). The Remote Access listener (internal/remote) adds CP-49 bounds, public-name Host check and per-client limits. Missing: the UDS harness listener (CP-02 profile), per-source connection and unauthenticated-work limits on the MCP endpoint, nftables rules on remote enable (SR-4.14-1). Deferred from 1.0 (SRS Appendix N): the mTLS Harness Profile.

elements.name: Protocol Mediator
elements.note: Both protocol eras through the MCP Go SDK in stateless mode, method allowlist, cache hints, Appendix B codes with reasonCode, correlationId, decisionId and the data.message text (FR-1.51), hold-mode keep-alives, list_changed on listen streams after policy activation. Backend progress is relayed with the northbound token: strictly increasing, at most 10 per second per request (CP-21), nothing after the response, each message through the response filters. Server-initiated requests other than ping get -32601 (FR-5.20) and an InputRequiredResult maps to -31010 (FR-5.24). Missing: trace-context and clientInfo capture (FR-1.44, FR-1.45), -32600 for batches and 202 for unknown notifications (FR-1.4, FR-1.5), the listen-stream limit (FR-1.38), keep-alives on idle listen streams. Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): the MRTR Relay Profile.

elements.name: Identity & Authentication Service
elements.note: OAuth 2.1 authorization server (metadata, PKCE S256, resource, iss), pre-registered clients, sign-in by Session Approver accounts only (the Administrator is refused), Argon2id, rate limits, lockout with backoff and dummy verification; a second redemption of an authorization code ends the session the first created (AUTH_CODE_REUSE). Principals and OAuth client credentials created from the control API (internal/principals, G-11) are found next to those of smcp.toml; suspending a principal refuses new sessions and revoking a credential ends its sessions. Remote Access adds RFC 7591 registration with operator approval, the RFC 8628 device grant and a cross-client Session Approver lockout. Missing: Client ID Metadata Document fetching with the CP-52 allowlist, UDS peer credentials. Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): mTLS client authentication.

elements.name: Session Manager
elements.note: Session store with CP-18 lifetimes, per-principal limits, scope-to-template mapping, session API, refresh-token rotation with reuse detection, janitors, per-session lifetime and allowed templates for remote sessions; operators can suspend and resume a session (FR-2.8), which refuses its tokens and calls until resumed. Session taint is tracked by the policy layer. Missing: sessions, taint state, rate windows and quotas are in memory and do not survive a restart (FR-2.16); no baseline context key at session creation (FR-2.13).

elements.name: Policy Administration Service
elements.note: Signed Policy Store (Ed25519, immutable revision files named by digest, signed active record with atomic activation), start-up import and fail-closed verification, publish with optional parent check, rollback as a new revision, diff, simulation from the journal or fixtures, /api/v1/policy* and smcpctl policy. Audit Profiles, Observation Policies and Anomaly Response Policies are published as numbered revisions by internal/obspolicy, outside the signed policy document. Missing: draft workspace (FR-3.3), those object types inside the policy document (FR-3.1), manifest ceiling checks at publication (SR-1-1, SR-1-3), overlap analysis (SR-1.9-1), stored fixture sets, import as draft.

elements.name: Policy Decision Service
elements.note: Default-deny decisions with deny-rule precedence, restrict-only session taint (TAINT_APPROVAL, TAINT_DENIED), sliding-window rates with CP-11 burst, per-session quotas, CP-12 evaluation bounds, filter obligations, profile and template intersection, Diff and Simulate. A build tag smcp_broken produces a deliberately defective decider for the FR-15.8 broken-build check; release builds never set it. Missing: argument predicates (FR-3.6), approval floor by side-effect class (SR-1.18-1), decision explanation route (SR-1.19-1), permits bound to revision IDs (SR-1.6-1), secret-use, egress and runtime obligations (FR-3.12); quotas count permitted decisions rather than completed calls.

elements.name: Approval Service
elements.note: Persisted one-use approvals bound per SR-1.18-2, CP-17 expiry, hold mode with keep-alives and the -31002 fallback carrying approvalId, expiresAt and approvalUrl, Approver accounts, /api/v1/approvals* with a watch stream that ends when its token ends, the harness status route, smcpctl approvals, desktop notification, G-13 console view, optional anomaly-band approval obligation. Approval events of remote calls carry the remote origin fields. The real-agent suite holds and approves a call from each passing client, and a recorded Claude Code run covers the four FR-3.25 cases (approve from G-13, approve with smcpctl, deny, hold bound); approval errors carry the approval text in error.message, which Claude Code shows. Missing: anomaly evidence shown to the Approver (FR-3.18), re-approval after a transforming filter (SR-1.18-3).

elements.name: Access Enforcement Point
elements.note: Session-scoped catalog per policy revision, updated in place on policy activation, unknown-tool rejection, approval hint (FR-1.50), metadata rule-set screen at presentation (FR-1.52). Catalogs built before a revision is suspended keep listing its tools until rebuilt (calls are refused). Missing: HMAC-protected pagination cursors (SR-5.7-2), the gateway-admin class (SR-3.12-1), keeping valid data: icons (SR-5.18-2). Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): manifest handle contracts (SR-2.12-1).

elements.name: Request Inspection Pipeline
elements.note: Ordered request chain with mandatory and policy-obliged filters, CP-14 deadline, panic as block: schema-validate (the schema compiler loads no external $ref and a schema that has one fails closed), size-limit, unicode-control, secret-fingerprint, path-canonicalize, url-canonicalize, injection-detect (tag only), the vault's secret-in-arguments filter; versioned rule sets with digests and measured error rates. Missing: data-class rules (SR-5.8-1), a second decision after a transforming filter (SR-5.12-1), request scoring as a stage.

elements.name: Tool Dispatcher
elements.note: stdio dispatch with CP-10 concurrency and queue bounds, CP-13 upstream timeout, bounded result reading, backend error mapping, suspension of a server on drift. No client capability is declared southbound (SR-5.6-2); server-initiated requests other than ping are refused with -32601 and an InputRequiredResult with -31010. Backend progress travels on a Gateway-issued token, routed in line order through a bounded queue. An instance that times out or fails is replaced and later calls wait for the new one; a relaunch that fails or shows another revision suspends the server. Instances are shared across sessions. Missing: per-session and per-call instances, cancellation propagation to the backend (FR-5.26), nesting-depth bound while reading. Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): the modern-era southbound probe and requests (FR-5.16 to FR-5.18) and southbound Streamable HTTP (FR-5.28 to FR-5.31).

elements.name: Response Inspection Pipeline
elements.note: Response chain: size-limit (size and depth), output-schema, content-type-gate, secret-fingerprint (redact or withhold with SECRET_LEAK), unicode-control, pii-detect, injection-marker, delimit-untrusted (FR-4.18), the vault's leak filter; provenance with disposition and tags. Relayed progress messages pass the same chain: blocked ones are dropped, transformed ones are relayed as transformed, each with provenance. Missing: response scoring as a stage, a test per malformed result envelope (SR-5.20-1).

elements.name: Enforcement Coordinator
elements.note: One-use launch capability bound to correlation, decision, policy revision and tool; pre-launch and pre-release rechecks under the barrier; authorized committed with fsync before the capability and delivered before release; emergency stop and health gate refuse calls. SR-6.2-1 and SR-7.10-1 remain partial: the graph mirror is not consulted and not every recovery path is tested. A failed intent commit is refused with AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE rather than the Appendix B JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE.

elements.name: Library Trust Verifier
elements.note: Recipes, package build (npm, PyPI, OCI or binary by digest, locked dependency closure, live probe, Appendix J manifest), minisign signing and offline verification, trust anchors scoped to risk classes, revocation entries, library scan and import with receipts, artifact re-verification before every launch; bootstrap packages the reference server; reference packages for filesystem, git, fetch and memory are built, signed, imported and called by the reference-packages workflow. Missing: OCI registry library (FR-5.1), revocation feed staleness alert (SR-3-4), OCI probe without Podman, probe network isolation in Standalone.

elements.name: Local Server Registry
elements.note: Content-addressed artifact store, immutable revisions and registry states, enablement checks (Standalone refuses high risk, alias uniqueness, expiry), drift detection at start and on list_changed that suspends the revision, /api/v1/packages, smcpctl package and the G-10 view (enable, suspend, retire). A tool-name collision (FR-1.49) disables only the colliding revision, with a reason naming both tools and a SERVER_NOT_ENABLED event; the Gateway still starts. Missing: classification overrides (SR-3.11-1); era consistency at start (FR-5.17) is deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N). A revision enabled while smcpd runs is launched at the next start.

elements.name: Server Runtime Manager
elements.note: Launch specification from configuration, rootless Podman launcher (Enforced) and subprocess launcher (Standalone), environment allowlist, bounded stderr (start errors quote at most 2 KiB of it, with delivered secret values redacted), FR-5.27 shutdown sequence, reaping of leftover containers. An instance that times out or exits is relaunched; a failed relaunch suspends the server. Missing: launch specification from manifests, per-session and per-call instance scopes (FR-5.10), idle teardown and reuse (FR-5.11), a crash-loop threshold (FR-5.12).

elements.name: Execution Sandbox
elements.note: Rootless Podman with read-only root, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, default seccomp, distinct user namespace per instance, private namespaces, CP-24 cgroup limits, size-bounded tmpfs, grant-only mounts. network = egress attaches the instance to the Egress Broker on slirp4netns with nftables in the container's namespace that allow only TCP to its broker listeners. S3 secret files are mounted read-only at /smcp/secrets, which needs userns = keep-id. packaging/linux installs identities, nftables, systemd units and an AppArmor profile for smcpd (enforce mode); CI runs smcpd.service under real systemd with a sandboxed tool call. Missing: an AppArmor or SELinux profile for server containers, the smcp-srv identity (servers run under smcp-core).

elements.name: Runtime Monitor
elements.note: Runtime Monitor: cgroup sampling and inotify on memory and PID events, podman events, process_created, deviation (UNDECLARED_PROCESS, EXEC_INTO_INSTANCE), limit_breach, instance_killed and instance_exited evidence, alert and kill-instance actions. Missing: observation of file opens outside mounts and of network attempts (prevented, not observed), suspend-revision and suspend-session actions (FR-5.35), rules from manifests.

elements.name: Egress Broker
elements.note: Per-instance forward proxy (CONNECT with SNI check, plain HTTP), per-destination TLS-originating endpoints, grants by host, port, method and class, broker DNS with rebinding defense, reserved-address refusal, size, duration and rate limits, public-fetch profile, egress evidence, /api/v1/egress and smcpctl egress. Enforced for sandboxed servers: the Podman launcher attaches each egress instance and confines its namespace to the broker's listeners. S1 header injection on endpoint requests for the Secret Broker. Missing: grants from policy obligations, one-use egress capabilities (SR-5.16-1), outbound secret-fingerprint scanning (SR-5.8-2); advisory only in Standalone.

elements.name: Secret Vault
elements.note: Age-encrypted versioned vault, master key in the macOS Keychain or passphrase-wrapped, owner-only file modes, rotation with CP-15 overlap and retirement, smcpctl secrets and /api/v1/secrets (metadata only). Missing: master key under the E-22 key manager (SR-2.13-1), a vault health check (FR-7.11). Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): TPM key sealing.

elements.name: Secret Broker
elements.note: Secret Use Policy file, S1 header injection through the Egress Broker (including for sandboxed servers with network = egress), S2 per-call files, S3 per-instance files (mounted read-only into the sandbox), S4 environment with waiver, secret_use evidence without values, HMAC leak fingerprints for the filters, leak suspension and resume, withdrawal on emergency stop. Missing: withdrawal of launch-time deliveries when the artifact check suspends a revision, Secret Use Policies inside the signed policy document, withdrawal on session end, evidence redaction by E-21 and E-29.

elements.name: Audit & Evidence Service
elements.note: Signed hash-chained JSON Lines journal with group-committed fsync, crash recovery, signed anchor, verifier that follows evidence-key transitions, evidence export of closed segments, CP-27 unsigned-age rule, non-blocking observers feeding the graph mirror and observation. A failed write fails the endpoint closed. Missing: anchor rollback detection without off-host export, journal index for queries (FR-11.8), redaction of secret material in event details.

elements.name: Key & Trust Anchor Manager
elements.note: CP-53 server CA (365 days, path length 0, dNSName constraints) and listener certificate (90 days, renewed at 30), hot reload, CA rotation with overlap, evidence-key rotation with signed transition, policy-signing key, package trust anchors, operator token, installation ID; smcpd refuses to start when the operator token or a private key file is readable by group or others. smcpd warns when an older CA still has iPAddress constraints, which BoringSSL clients reject. Missing: a client CA, separate keys for every purpose listed by the SRS; the remote listener does not reload its certificate after rotation. Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): TPM and Keychain sealing of private keys (FR-7.9).

elements.name: Health & Safety Monitor
elements.note: Health and Safety Monitor with one-second checks, fail-closed latch with 10 s recovery and acknowledgment of integrity causes, edge gate, loopback Prometheus metrics with a loopback Host check, rotating redacted diagnostic log, profile decision with the not-enforced label. The graph mirror and the Observation Store register health checks that report degraded, never fail-closed. Missing: health checks for the vault and the memory stage (FR-7.11).

elements.name: Management Console & Control API
elements.note: smcpctl covers bootstrap, install, configuration, journal, policy, approvals, packages, trust, filters, secrets, egress, runtime, graph, observe, keys, backup, restore, upgrade, uninstall, remote, clients, lockdown and doctor. Control API with every Appendix C role from one route matrix and GET /api/v1/openapi.json describing every route (also rendered on the project site). Embedded React console with views G-01 to G-14 under a strict CSP: HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie sessions with a CSRF token and If-Match preconditions, G-11 principal and credential management with session suspension, and Audit Profiles, Observation Policies, Anomaly Response Policies and memory budgets published from G-03, G-04, G-06 and G-08 as numbered revisions applied at the next start. Playwright runs every view on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA checks. Missing: per-object If-Match revisions, the two latest releases of each browser (FR-8.30), the G-04 usability measure, immediate application of published observation objects.

elements.name: Graph Database Engine
elements.note: Neo4j Community Edition 2026.05.0 integration, disabled unless [graph] enabled: ordered migrations with uniqueness constraints for every Appendix D label, engine settings and heap checks against CP-33, smcpctl graph config. Missing: nftables rules for the engine port and outbound denial, page-cache measurement and the FR-9.12 degradation order.

elements.name: Data Access Service
elements.note: Data Access Service with a digest-checked template catalog, declared and bound parameters, server-side timeouts; the evidence mirror is an idempotent audit observer with journal catch-up and rebuild; /api/v1/graph* and canned queries. Missing: priority classes, observation batching and backpressure (FR-9.4 to FR-9.6), mirroring of Policy Store and registry contents beyond IDs on events. Deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N): peer credentials of the Data Access Service (SR-4.3-1).

elements.name: Observation Store
elements.note: Observation Store tables partitioned by UTC day with one column per catalog parameter, write-once batches, DuckDB with zstd Parquet (cgo builds) or JSON Lines (release archives), aggregate queries with parity between backends, CP-25 retention, a published memory budget (G-08). Missing: quotas; release archives built without cgo have no Parquet. Storage tiering (FR-9.13) is deferred from 1.0 (Appendix N).

elements.name: Data Lifecycle & Memory Manager
elements.note: Graph retention in bounded batches, heap sampling with pressure flag, DuckDB memory limit, observation retention, encrypted online backup and verified restore (smcpctl backup, restore). Missing: memory manager and degradation order, scheduled backups (FR-9.16), graph dump in backups and mirror rebuild on restore.

elements.name: Observation Collector
elements.note: Observation Collector as an audit observer plus mandatory probes: one record per call with the computed catalog parameters, deterministic sampling, capture escalation, drop counting, meta-metrics; never blocks a call. A published Observation Policy (scope by principal, framework type, template, server and tool; parameters, sampling, per-band escalation, contexts, bands) replaces the [observation] settings at the next start. Missing: per-stage and per-rule spans with CPU time (FR-10.2), observables from the other elements (FR-10.1), S3 payload capture, session records, first-N-per-session capture.

elements.name: Behavior Baseline Engine
elements.note: Welford statistics with optional decay, log1p and Box-Cox transforms, t-digest median and MAD, category and transition surprise, learning exclusions, sealed snapshots, drift reports, promotion and rollback, integrity events. Baseline contexts and bands come from the published Observation Policy, applied at the next start. Missing: contexts and thresholds from the signed policy document, a baseline context key per session (FR-2.13).

elements.name: Anomaly Scorer
elements.note: Digest-verified atomic snapshot load, z and robust z with sigma floors, max-|z| combination naming the feature, CP-30 bands and uncharacterized, asynchronous alerts and capture escalation, optional synchronous approval and withhold obligations (off by default), per-band actions from the published Anomaly Response Policy (restrict-only, lower bands may stay alert-only, the uncharacterized state maps to record, escalate or approve; applied at the next start). Missing: Anomaly Response Policies inside the signed policy document, anomaly evidence on the approval record.

elements.name: Research Dataset Service
elements.note: Campaign life cycle with clocks and quota, exports in Parquet, CSV, JSON Lines and GraphML with per-dataset HMAC pseudonyms, dictionary, manifest and checksums, CSV formula neutralization, export files opened inside their root. Researcher accounts create, submit and stop campaigns and export their datasets. Missing: a pseudonymization key issued by E-22, Parquet in builds without cgo.

elements.name: Harness Adapter Kit
elements.note: smcp-session, smcp-stdio (both eras, UDS dialing) and smcp-connect (binary and npm) with the CP-43 credential file; smcpctl clients setup, lockdown and doctor for the seven local clients; Tailscale Funnel and Cloudflare tunnel drivers. The real-agent suite passes Claude Code, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, OpenCode and Goose on all six scenarios, and its broken-build check turns Claude Code to fail against a deliberately broken smcpd. Gemini CLI is not run (no GEMINI_API_KEY; the AI Gateway does not serve the Gemini API) and Grok Build is not run (no public CLI). Missing: setup and lockdown runs at pinned versions (FR-15.8 for the adapters), dated cloud-agent runs for Grok Bot, ChatGPT and Meta Muse (FR-15.9), nftables rules on remote enable (SR-4.14-1).
